key_insight: HVAF-sprayed Tribaloy-400 forms a denser, more protective oxide layer than detonation-sprayed Tribaloy-400, giving better resistance to molten solar-salt corrosion at 500 °C.
engineering_relevance: For concentrated solar power thermal-storage containers, HVAF T-400 coatings appear more suitable than DS coatings for extending service life under long-term hot-corrosion exposure.
method: Tribaloy-400 was deposited on ASTM A516 steel using HVAF and detonation spraying.
Coated samples were exposed to 60% NaNO3–40% KNO3 molten salt at 500 °C for up to 1000 h.
Phase, SEM, and elemental-mapping analyses were used to compare oxide formation, salt ingress, and coating degradation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HVAF retained a uniform Cr–Mo–Si–O enriched surface with minimal salt penetration after 1000 h, while DS showed deeper salt ingress, higher mass gain, and more spallation.
watch_item: The result is specific to one coating composition, one substrate, and one molten-salt chemistry, so performance may differ under other CSP operating conditions.
paper_title: Hot corrosion behavior of thermal sprayed using HVAF and DS techniques with Tribaloy-400 coatings for solar energy storage container
